steps.description: Build a DESeqDataSet from counts.csv and metadata.csv with design = ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, genotype releveled to WT reference and treatment releveled to vehicle reference (explicit, reported). Pre-filter genes to >=10 counts in >=4 samples (the smallest cell size). Run DESeq() with median-of-ratios normalization built into the model (no pre-normalization of counts). Extract three results tables: (1) the interaction coefficient genotypeKO.treatmentdrug via results(name=...) — the direct test of 'does the drug act differently in KO vs WT'; (2) the simple effect of treatment (drug vs vehicle) in WT via the treatment_drug_vs_vehicle main-effect coefficient; (3) the simple effect of treatment in KO via list(c('treatment_drug_vs_vehicle','genotypeKO.treatmentdrug')). Apply apeglm shrinkage to each of the three coefficients (each is a single model coefficient, so apeglm applies). Flag and report NA p-values from Cook's-distance count-outlier handling per DESeq2 default (n=4/cell is under the 7-replicate threshold, so outliers are flagged not replaced). Inspect the raw p-value histogram for each of the three contrasts before adjustment. Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within each contrast separately at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering on. Produce MA plots and the dispersion plot as fit diagnostics.

plan.title: 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is the classic 2x2 factorial interaction question. Design is genotype (WT, KO) x treatment (vehicle, drug), 4 replicates per cell, 16 samples, raw salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 17 columns incl. gene symbol; metadata 16x4). We fit a single DESeq2 model with design ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, test the interaction coefficient (genotypeKO.treatmentdrug) first — this is the direct answer to 'does the drug act differently in KO vs WT' — then report the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT, and within KO) so a reader can see the direction and magnitude behind the interaction. QC precedes modeling to catch outliers or batch-like structure the profile does not already flag. Low-count pre-filtering is minimal (independent filtering handles the rest). LFC shrinkage uses apeglm per single coefficient (each simple effect and the interaction term is one coefficient in this 2-level x 2-level design, so apeglm applies, not ashr, which is reserved for multi-coefficient contrasts). BH-FDR at alpha 0.05 is applied within each of the three contrasts separately. Enrichment (fgsea preranked on the Wald statistic) runs per contrast against MSigDB Hallmark first, then Reactome, both confirmed present in the reference store for human. The final report assembles the three-contrast table side by side plus fit diagnostics, exactly as the interaction-design reporting rule requires.

design = ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, explicit reference levels (WT, vehicle)

apeglm shrinkage for each single-coefficient simple effect and the interaction coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast, alpha=0.05, independent filtering on
fgsea preranked on Wald stat, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome, per contrast
Report simple effects + interaction contrast side by side, diagnostics, session info
